scope.summary: Implement futa/mixed anatomy support (spec 13.21; REQ-035): female body plus penis module coexistence in one BodySpec genital config with isolated channel namespaces, watertight composite mesh, and zero cross-module conflicts - archetype (h) futa cross-blend is an acceptance body and uses the same engines with no special-case forks.
acceptance_criteria: Futa config: the BodySpec genital config allows vulva and penis modules active simultaneously in a documented anatomically-composited layout; the resulting mesh stays watertight and manifold.
Channel namespace isolation: penis_* and vulva/labia_* channel groups coexist with zero cross-writes, proven by a BODY_DECOUPLE_VALID matrix run over the mixed config (REQ-035).
The masc/fem continuum channel (MT-510) composes with the mixed genital config: feminine body + oversized erect penis (archetype h) passes mesh-quality and pose gates.
No special-case forks: the same skinning, corrective, and skin-blend paths handle mixed anatomy unchanged.
scope.risk_if_missed: Futa is a standing market category (the Futalicious ecosystem is the proof) and archetype (h) is a named acceptance body; namespace collisions or code forks here would break the decouple law and double the maintenance surface of every genital path.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Backend/solver scope: behavior is observable via TraceProjection, typed TAILOR_BODY_* receipts, and the 13.12 capture APIs; operator/model GUI exposure rides the BodyKit panes (13.27) and is validated there.

target_entries: Tailor UserManual > BodyKit genital anatomy and controls

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: This MT owns authoritative, job, or external-tool lifecycle events and must project the same event_id, run_id, actor_id, and correlation_id from EventLedger into Flight Recorder.
This MT emits typed diagnostics through its owning command or job and inherits retention, health, and projection behavior from the shared diagnostics substrate.
The owning native shell or scheduled job supplies Palmistry coverage; this MT must preserve operation identity and recovery handles.

risks: Broad MT scope can hide multiple review targets.
Markdown MT lists may disagree with packet-declared active/next MT truth.
Receipt routing may target an old MT if contract identity is omitted.
minimum_controls: Exactly one primary proof target per MT unless the packet records why not.
MT identity must be stable and referenced by receipt correlation.
Generated projection drift must not wake Coder or Validator by itself.

required_changes_before_execution: Consume the signed technical refinement, canonical command/surface registries, classified HBR tiers, and task-oriented UserManual contract before execution.
